title: The derived tensor product on the finite-Tor subcategories
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, $n\geq1$, put
$A=A_{E,n}$, and let $X$ be a
finite-type
$k$-scheme. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ have
finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$,
and let $M\in D^b_c(X,A)$ be
bounded constructible.
Then:

1. **(i)** $K\otimes_A^LM$ belongs to $D^b_c(X,A)$;
1. **(ii)** if in addition $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ has finite Tor amplitude
in $[c,d]$, then $K\otimes_A^LM$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, with
finite Tor amplitude in $[a+c,b+d]$.

proof.text: Work on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with the constant ring sheaf $A_X$. Since $X$ is a $k$-scheme of characteristic $p$ and $\ell\ne p$, $\ell$ is invertible on $X$. By [lem-sf-flat-model], choose a complex $P$ of flat $A_X$-module sheaves concentrated in $[a,b]$ and an isomorphism $K\cong P$ in the derived category. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] to the ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_X)$: $P$ is bounded above by $b$, so it is K-flat. The computation of [def-weil-derived-tensor], together with invariance under derived isomorphisms from [lem-weil-derived-tensor-functorial], therefore computes $K\otimes_A^L M$ by $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_A M_0)$ for any representative complex $M_0$ of $M$.

For (i), [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] gives integers $c'<d'$ such that $\mathcal H^i(M)=0$ outside $[c',d']$. From any representative $M_0$ form its good upper truncation $B=\tau_{\le d'}M_0$, with $B^{d'}=\ker(d_{M_0}^{d'})$, unchanged terms below $d'$, and zero terms above. Form $C=\tau_{\ge c'}B$, with $C^{c'}=\operatorname{coker}(d_B^{c'-1})$, unchanged terms above $c'$, and zero terms below. The inclusion $B\to M_0$ preserves cohomology in degrees at most $d'$ and removes only the zero cohomology in degrees above $d'$. Since $c'<d'$, the projection $B\to C$ preserves cohomology in degrees at least $c'$ (at $c'$ it identifies both cohomology sheaves with $\ker(d_B^{c'})/\operatorname{im}(d_B^{c'-1})$) and removes only the zero cohomology below $c'$. Thus both maps are quasi-isomorphisms. Hence $C$ represents $M$ and is concentrated in $[c',d']$. By step 1 the tensor is represented by $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_A C)$. Its degree-$t$ term is $\bigoplus_{q+r=t}P^q\otimes_A C^r$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], which is zero outside $[a+c',b+d']$. Thus the tensor has bounded cohomology.

For constructibility in (i), apply [lem-pur-finite-tensor-constructible-cohomology] with $T=X$, $L=M$ and the given $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Its hypotheses hold: $n\ge1$, $\ell$ is invertible on $X$ by step 1, and $K$ and $M$ are bounded constructible in the intrinsic finite-torsion category (membership in $D^b_{ctf}$ includes membership in $D^b_c$). It states that every cohomology sheaf of $K\otimes_A^L M$ is constructible on the pro-etale site. With boundedness from step 2, the defining condition [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] proves $K\otimes_A^L M\in D^b_c(X,A)$.

For (ii), [lem-sf-flat-model] applied to $M$ supplies a flat complex $Q$ concentrated in $[c,d]$ and isomorphic to $M$ in the derived category. The computation of [def-weil-derived-tensor] and functoriality [lem-weil-derived-tensor-functorial] represent $K\otimes_A^L M$ by $R=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_A Q)$. By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], $R^t=\bigoplus_{q+r=t}P^q\otimes_A Q^r$. Each summand is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]: its tensor functor is, by tensor associativity, the composite of the two exact tensor functors for $P^q$ and $Q^r$. There are only finitely many nonzero summands in each total degree. Tensoring a finite direct sum is the finite direct sum of those tensor functors. Applied to a short exact sequence, its kernel and cokernel are the direct sums of the summand kernels and cokernels, so the result remains short exact. Thus $R^t$ is flat. A nonzero summand requires $a\le q\le b$ and $c\le r\le d$, hence $a+c\le t\le b+d$. Thus $R$ is a bounded flat model in $[a+c,b+d]$. The tensor is already bounded constructible by (i), so the reverse implication of [lem-sf-flat-model] gives its Tor amplitude in this interval. Together these prove membership in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.
